chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the visitation (to the Kaaba) after the pilgrimage visitation during the days of Tashriq, and he said, 'No.' This does not contradict what we mentioned, because he negated it in the sense of being preferable and more appropriate, rather than prohibition or obligation. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ الْحَجِّ: The visitation associated with the Hajj pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden to visit the Kaaba again after Hajg during the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to a query about performing a second visitation to the Kaaba during the days of Tashriq with a simple 'No.' The scholar clarifies that this is a ruling of *fada'il* (superiority/preference) rather than *hadr* (prohibition), indicating that while permissible, it is not the optimal course of action compared to other recommended acts or resting. This distinction highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudential approach to distinguishing between obligatory prohibitions and recommended preferences in ritual practices.
